verdict.rationale: Metorial documents session-level tool filters with an explicit allowlist mode ("type": "allow" with tool keys), so individual tools can be restricted per provider. Server-level restriction comes from approved integrations in Workforce portals, alongside stated access controls and RBAC. missing for 10: in-depth docs on admin-enforced per-agent or per-user tool policies (beyond developer-set session filters), deny-mode and policy-precedence details, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can restrict which servers and individual tools an agent may call through allowlists or per-tool access control

citations.quote: Tool filters let you control which tools from a provider are available during a session.
Portals are branded places where users discover and connect approved integrations, skills, and MCP access.
Let your team connect AI agents and MCP clients like Cursor, ChatGPT, and Claude to approved apps, tools, and shared skills, with access controls and activity logs.
RBAC, SAML SSO, and IAM built in so agent access follows your existing security model.
